contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #107: Matrix multiplication with exponent at most 9/4.
Extend the staged complex nine-fourths polynomial-profile construction to exact scalar arithmetic over every fixed field F.

definitions.restriction: A tensor B is an F-linear restriction of A if independent F-linear substitutions on the three legs transform A into B.
definitions.omega_F: Infimum of exponents tau giving O_epsilon(n^(tau+epsilon)) exact scalar-arithmetic matrix multiplication over a fixed field F for every epsilon>0.
definitions.finite_extension_cost: Number of full direct-sum source copies used to descend an extension-linear restriction to F.

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 107 (Matrix multiplication with exponent at most 9/4.; papers: An Upper Bound of 9/4 for the Matrix Multiplication Exponent; Complex Matrix Multiplication Below 2.258 and Rectangular Bounds; Staggered extraction for exact matrix multiplication over every field; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/107.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
For every fixed field F and epsilon>0, two n by n matrices over F can be multiplied using O_(F,epsilon)(n^(9/4+epsilon)) exact scalar arithmetic operations.

For every finite field extension E/F of degree e, every E-linear restriction A_E >= B_E between F-defined tensors descends to an F-linear restriction A^(direct-sum e^2) >= B. If A_E^tensor-j >= B_E^tensor-j for a fixed E and arbitrary j, the descent cost is e^2, not e^(2j). No separability hypothesis is needed.

If F-defined tensors A and B admit a polynomial degeneration over a finite extension E/F, then lambda_F(A)>=lambda_F(B) for every F-tensor character. For degree D and power j, at most (jD+1)(e s_j)^2 full copies suffice, where s_j=1 over infinite E and s_j=ceil(log_(|E|)(jD+2)) over finite E.

For matched blocks sharing the first leg, choose L in {5M,5M+1} not divisible by char(F); Fourier separation over F(zeta_L), followed by degeneration, implies the same shared-leg entropy inequality as in the staged complex proof. Take the tensor-power interpolation limit at fixed type length before the type-length limit.

For every field F, the integral basis Q_i=S_i, Q_(e+1)=W_e, K_j=W_j-S_(j+1) gives the determinant filtration simultaneously for all first-input multiplication slices and implies 2P(a,b)>=P(a,b+1)+P(a,b-1).

For every field F, the staged three-sector degeneration has no negative-weight supported terms; its middle branch is C(a,h) with second and third legs exchanged and first-leg basis reversed, yielding P(a,3h+a-1)>=3P(a,h).
For every F-tensor character, convolution has value at most a+b-1 via finite-extension descent; its balanced profile satisfies P(a,a)>=a^(4/3), and hence lambda(T_d)<=d^(9/4).
For every field F, with nu_F=inf_(n>=2) log_n rank_F(T_n), every integer d>=2 and 0<=k<d^(nu_F) admit an F-tensor character lambda with lambda(T_d)>=k.
Bounding every F-tensor character by lambda(T_d)<=d^(9/4) implies nu_F<=9/4 by detecting characters, and exact block recursion over F gives omega_F<=9/4.

claims.natural_statement: For arbitrary fields F,E with an F-algebra structure and a finite F-basis b indexed by D, any E-valued leg substitutions taking an F-source coefficient array to an F-target coefficient array admit a normalized F-linear functional and the explicit sum over D x D of F-restrictions of that same source; card(D x D)=card(D)^2. The same quantifiers cover all powered dimensions with the same basis.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Basis.VectorSpace
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dual.Lemmas
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

open scoped BigOperators
open Module

namespace AllFieldsNineFourths

variable {F E : Type*} [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]
variable {D I J K X Y Z : Type*}
variable [Fintype D] [Fintype I] [Fintype J] [Fintype K]

theorem normalized_functional :
    ∃ ell : E →ₗ[F] F, ell (1 : E) = 1 :=
  Module.Projective.exists_dual_eq_one F one_ne_zero

theorem functional_product_expansion
    (b : Basis D F E) (ell : E →ₗ[F] F) (x y z : E) :
    ell (x * y * z) =
      ∑ s, ∑ t, (b.repr x s * b.repr y t) * ell (b s * b t * z) := by
  conv_lhs => rw [← b.sum_repr x, ← b.sum_repr y]
  simp only [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum, smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm,
    map_sum, map_smul, smul_eq_mul, mul_assoc]

def restrictionCoefficient
    (a : I × J × K → F) (u : I → X → F)
    (v : J → Y → F) (w : K → Z → F) (x : X) (y : Y) (z : Z) : F :=
  ∑ q, a q * u q.1 x * v q.2.1 y * w q.2.2 z

def extensionRestrictionCoefficient
    (a : I × J × K → F) (u : I → X → E)
    (v : J → Y → E) (w : K → Z → E) (x : X) (y : Y) (z : Z) : E :=
  ∑ q, a q • (u q.1 x * v q.2.1 y * w q.2.2 z)

theorem sum_three_swap {T : Type*} [Fintype T] (f : T → D → D → F) :
    (∑ q, ∑ s, ∑ t, f q s t) = ∑ s, ∑ t, ∑ q, f q s t := by
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro s hs
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]

theorem restriction_descent_formula
    (b : Basis D F E) (ell : E →ₗ[F] F) (h_one : ell (1 : E) = 1)
    (a : I × J × K → F) (target : X → Y → Z → F)
    (u : I → X → E) (v : J → Y → E) (w : K → Z → E)
    (h : ∀ x y z, extensionRestrictionCoefficient a u v w x y z =
      target x y z • (1 : E)) (x : X) (y : Y) (z : Z) :
    target x y z =
      ∑ s, ∑ t, restrictionCoefficient a
        (fun i x => b.repr (u i x) s)
        (fun j y => b.repr (v j y) t)
        (fun k z => ell (b s * b t * w k z)) x y z := by
  have term (q : I × J × K) :
      ell (a q • (u q.1 x * v q.2.1 y * w q.2.2 z)) =
        ∑ s, ∑ t, a q * b.repr (u q.1 x) s * b.repr (v q.2.1 y) t *
          ell (b s * b t * w q.2.2 z) := by
    rw [map_smul, functional_product_expansion b ell]
    simp only [smul_eq_mul, Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]
  calc
    target x y z = ell (extensionRestrictionCoefficient a u v w x y z) := by
      rw [h, map_smul, h_one, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    _ = ∑ q, ∑ s, ∑ t,
        a q * b.repr (u q.1 x) s * b.repr (v q.2.1 y) t *
          ell (b s * b t * w q.2.2 z) := by
      rw [extensionRestrictionCoefficient, map_sum]
      exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun q _ => term q)
    _ = ∑ s, ∑ t, ∑ q,
        a q * b.repr (u q.1 x) s * b.repr (v q.2.1 y) t *
          ell (b s * b t * w q.2.2 z) := sum_three_swap _
    _ = _ := rfl

theorem finite_extension_restriction_descent
    (b : Basis D F E) (a : I × J × K → F) (target : X → Y → Z → F)
    (u : I → X → E) (v : J → Y → E) (w : K → Z → E)
    (h : ∀ x y z, extensionRestrictionCoefficient a u v w x y z =
      target x y z • (1 : E)) :
    ∃ ell : E →ₗ[F] F, ell (1 : E) = 1 ∧
      ∀ x y z, target x y z =
        ∑ s, ∑ t, restrictionCoefficient a
          (fun i x => b.repr (u i x) s)
          (fun j y => b.repr (v j y) t)
          (fun k z => ell (b s * b t * w k z)) x y z := by
  obtain ⟨ell, h_one⟩ := normalized_functional (F := F) (E := E)
  exact ⟨ell, h_one, restriction_descent_formula b ell h_one a target u v w h⟩

theorem number_of_source_copies :
    Fintype.card (D × D) = Fintype.card D ^ 2 := by
  simp [pow_two]

theorem mismatch_weight_identity {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (g h u v : R) :
    (g ^ 2 + h * u - h ^ 2 - h * v) - (g - h) ^ 2 =
      h * (u - v + 2 * (g - h)) := by
  ring

#print axioms finite_extension_restriction_descent
#print axioms mismatch_weight_identity

end AllFieldsNineFourths

  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl

  ring

    (a : I × J × K → F) (u : I → X → F)
    (v : J → Y → F) (w : K → Z → F) (x : X) (y : Y) (z : Z) : F :=

    (a : I × J × K → F) (u : I → X → E)
    (v : J → Y → E) (w : K → Z → E) (x : X) (y : Y) (z : Z) : E :=

theorem sum_three_swap {T : Type*} [Fintype T] (f : T → D → D → F) :

  rw [Finset.sum_comm]

    (b : Basis D F E) (ell : E →ₗ[F] F) (h_one : ell (1 : E) = 1)
    (a : I × J × K → F) (target : X → Y → Z → F)
    (u : I → X → E) (v : J → Y → E) (w : K → Z → E)
    (h : ∀ x y z, extensionRestrictionCoefficient a u v w x y z =
      target x y z • (1 : E)) (x : X) (y : Y) (z : Z) :
    target x y z =
      ∑ s, ∑ t, restrictionCoefficient a
        (fun i x => b.repr (u i x) s)
        (fun j y => b.repr (v j y) t)
        (fun k z => ell (b s * b t * w k z)) x y z := by
  have term (q : I × J × K) :
      ell (a q • (u q.1 x * v q.2.1 y * w q.2.2 z)) =
        ∑ s, ∑ t, a q * b.repr (u q.1 x) s * b.repr (v q.2.1 y) t *
          ell (b s * b t * w q.2.2 z) := by
    rw [map_smul, functional_product_expansion b ell]
    simp only [smul_eq_mul, Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]
  calc
    target x y z = ell (extensionRestrictionCoefficient a u v w x y z) := by
      rw [h, map_smul, h_one, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    _ = ∑ q, ∑ s, ∑ t,
        a q * b.repr (u q.1 x) s * b.repr (v q.2.1 y) t *
          ell (b s * b t * w q.2.2 z) := by
      rw [extensionRestrictionCoefficient, map_sum]
      exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun q _ => term q)
    _ = ∑ s, ∑ t, ∑ q,
        a q * b.repr (u q.1 x) s * b.repr (v q.2.1 y) t *

      target x y z • (1 : E)) :
    ∃ ell : E →ₗ[F] F, ell (1 : E) = 1 ∧
      ∀ x y z, target x y z =
        ∑ s, ∑ t, restrictionCoefficient a
          (fun i x => b.repr (u i x) s)
          (fun j y => b.repr (v j y) t)

routes.retired_because: Normalized trace is not a universal retraction: it vanishes identically on nontrivial purely inseparable extensions, and trace(1) can vanish in positive characteristic. Use an arbitrary F-linear functional ell with ell(1)=1 instead. This is a rejected proposed extension route, not a flaw in the complex-only manuscript.
